subject.title: refactor: move non-session runtime journals to SQLite

question: Should OpenClaw advance the per-agent database to schema v11 while replacing the existing ACP and memory-event inspection contracts in this release?
rationale: Repository policy requires explicit approval for SQLite schema-version bumps, and the permanent replacement shape for supported diagnostic access is a maintainer-owned compatibility decision.

options.title: Preserve access, then approve v11
options.body: Add supported SQLite-backed ACP and memory-event inspection contracts, migrate all writers and consumers, then approve the schema bump with upgrade proof.

options.title: Approve the breaking replacement
options.body: Intentionally remove the old contracts, document the upgrade break, and require explicit release and migration acceptance before merge.

options.title: Split the schema change
options.body: Land contract-preserving journal migrations separately and defer the ACP table and schema bump to a narrower reviewed PR.

recommendation.title: Preserve access, then approve v11
recommendation.body: Add supported SQLite-backed ACP and memory-event inspection contracts, migrate all writers and consumers, then approve the schema bump with upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged session/transcript SQLite work most directly established the database and upgrade architecture being extended.
